messages:
Sam H: ok quick sync — we need to pick a default for collector pipelines in the next config freeze. question: do we ship per-signal pipelines by default (traces/metrics/logs each isolated) or a single unified pipeline with routing rules? customers hit retention/quotas headaches and infra wants simpler memory bounds. thoughts?
Maria T: my instinct is per-signal by default. traces and metrics have very different batching/latency profiles. unified usually ends up with lots of special-casing. :thinking:
Alex P: per-signal makes ops easier for SLAs but increases config surface + UI complexity. can we do per-signal under the hood but show a single toggle in Console?
Katie L: +1 to Alex. UX should not force customers to care about pipelines unless they opt in. default 'smart split' maybe?
Jason R: operationally, we saw an outage where a heavy logs exporter caused span batching to starve and KV cache growth. that was unified pipeline + shared exporter. logs blew memory. snippet from kube OOM: `OOMKill - pid 2345 (otelcol), rss: 6.1GiB`
Ira S: can confirm. gateway collectors that handle multi-tenant traffic should isolate signals. sidecars can be simpler unified per-app. so default: agent-sidecar = unified, gateway = per-signal.
Sam H: that hybrid sounds promising. any rough perf/cost tradeoffs?
Maria T: per-signal gateway lets us size workers per signal. traces need more CPU for sampling and KV cache; metrics are bursty network I/O; logs are high throughput but simpler pipeline. our internal benchmarks show 30-40% cost savings when we tune batching per-signal vs one-size-fits-all.
Alex P: how about exporters? do we let customers attach exporters to each pipeline in Console? that needs UI for ordering and failover (eg OTLP -> backup -> S3).
Katie L: yes, and show quick defaults: `OTLP` for traces+metrics, `S3` or `GCS` for logs retention. Add a 'fallback route' toggle.
Sam H: proposal for config MVP:
1) Agent (sidecar) defaults to unified pipeline with sane batching and per-tenant quotas enforced at router layer.
2) Gateway defaults to per-signal pipelines. Console exposes an "Advanced pipelines" opt-in for agents to create per-signal splits.
3) Exporter config: per-pipeline list, with priority and retry/backoff settings.
4) Retention: Console shows estimated monthly cost for retention TTL changes and a per-route retention slider.

Can someone draft the OTEL snippet we'll use for docs?
Maria T: here's a minimal gateway example we can start with:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
      http: {}
processors:
  batch_traces:
    timeout: 200ms
  batch_metrics:
    timeout: 1s
pipelines:
  traces:
    receivers: [otlp]
    processors: [batch_traces]
    exporters: [otlp/jaeger]
  metrics:
    receivers: [otlp]
    processors: [batch_metrics]
    exporters: [otlp/prom]
exporters:
  otlp/jaeger:
    endpoint: jaeger-redwood.internal:14250
  otlp/prom:
    endpoint: prom-remote:4317
```
Alex P: looks good. two followups: how do we handle quotas? token-based per-tenant counters at routing layer or sampler-level?
Ira S: do quotas at the gateway router before pipelines — cheap and prevents wasted CPU/batching. allow soft quotas that sample traces when overage, hard quotas drop logs/metrics.
Katie L: need telemetry to show 'quota burn rate' per-route in Console. customers ask for alerts when retention spend > threshold.
Jason R: about rollouts — we should A/B the per-signal pipelines behind a feature flag for a few big customers. small percentage traffic to new pipeline, measure latency, error rate, and cost delta. deploy-bot can do a canary.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollout for `gateway-per-signal` flag at 2024-12-05T15:00Z by @deploy-bot. :rocket:
Sam H: acceptance criteria for MVP:
- no regressions in 99th percentile latency for traces in canary group
- <1% increase in ops incidents related to collector memory in first month
- Console exposes a single toggle + advanced per-signal editor
- retention cost estimates visible before saving changes

Any objections?
Maria T: none, but add migration docs: how to split pipelines without losing telemetry (exporter dup rules, temporary fanout).
Alex P: also include a CLI config converter: `redwoodctl collector split-pipelines --from unified --to per-signal` to automate migration.
Katie L: UI note: default view should show "Recommended config" that applies safe batching/retention. advanced users can edit raw OTEL yaml.
Ira S: logging: add enforcement metrics so we can surface exporter backpressure and queue sizes.
Sam H: great — I'll open a GH PR with the proposal and link to this thread. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
